piece.title: String Quartet in E-flat major
piece.why: Fanny Hensel's Romanza: Violin I states the theme, the viola echoes a phrase, then the cello restates the theme in its high tenor register under a Violin I countermelody.

roster.label: Church brass: 2 trumpets (one beginner), horn, euphonium

plan.summary: The 1st trumpet carries the tune the whole way: the Violin 1 melody in bars 1–12, then the same theme when the cello takes it back in bars 13–16. The euphonium holds the bass throughout. It starts on the low G pedal (from Violin 2) in bar 1, plays the cello line through bar 12, then the viola's held low notes. The horn plays the viola's inner line, then the Violin 1 countermelody briefly. The beginner 2nd trumpet plays the easiest repeated-note accompaniment in the bars that fit its small range.

assignments.reason: The main tune (Violin 1), an octave down so it fits the trumpet. The bright sound keeps it on top.
The tune continues. These bars drop to D4, so they are played at written pitch to stay in the trumpet's range.
The tune climbs to A-flat here, so it goes back down an octave to fit the trumpet.
The cello brings the opening theme back. The 1st trumpet follows the tune, and it fits at written pitch.
The cello's repeated B-flats sit over the low G pedal. It's an easy, in-range entry for the beginner.
Violin 2 held notes and simple eighths, all in the beginner's comfortable range.
Violin 2 repeated-note accompaniment, all within B-flat3 to B-flat4.
The viola's inner line. The horn blends under the trumpet, and the whole line fits its range.
The Violin 1 countermelody over the returning theme, an octave down to suit the horn. Here it stays above the bass.
Violin 2's low G is the real bass in bar 1, under the cello's B-flats, so the euphonium holds it.
The cello bass at written pitch, so it doesn't sink under Violin 2's low notes. The one or two notes above F4 are moved down by the checker. [checker moved this line -1 octave(s) to fit the range]
The cello sits high in this bar. An octave down keeps the bass under the trumpet's tune. [checker moved this line +1 octave(s) to fit the range]
The cello bass and its low G pedal at written pitch. The one low E sits inside the pedal, and the checker moves it up. [checker moved this line +1 octave(s) to fit the range]
The cello's high E-flat pickup goes down an octave, so it stays under the trumpet's tune leading into bar 9. [checker moved this line +1 octave(s) to fit the range]
The descending cello bass at written pitch. The few top notes in bar 12 are moved down by the checker, and the rest stays under the accompaniment.
The viola's held G's and D's are the bass here while the cello has the tune. The euphonium stays on the bottom.

dropped.reason: Violin 2 filler goes up to C5–E5, past the beginner's B-flat4. The harmony is still covered by the horn and euphonium, and no other player is free.
This passage spans G3 to E-flat5, too wide for the beginner. It is accompaniment only.
This bar reaches C5 and B4, above the beginner's range. It is filler only.
Inner filler that goes up to G5, too high for the beginner. Played an octave down, it would fall below the bass, and all other players are busy.
An octave down, the countermelody falls under the returning theme, and at written pitch it's too high for the horn. The theme and bass carry these bars.
